issues.title: E5 · Reliability at scale (epic)
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** R1–R5 (PRD 7.6, ARCHITECTURE 13)
### Summary
Reliability at scale: piece hashes, any holder sends any piece, spreading, chaos tests and a dashboard, repair pieces. Children: #78 (ask another holder), #79 (a hash for every piece) and #80 (chaos options). R3 and R5 get tickets once R4's numbers say they're needed.

issues.title: F18 · Drags stay clear of the phone's own gestures
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** F18
### Summary
Dragging can trigger the back swipe or a pull-down panel on phones.
### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)
Nothing dragged needs to start within 24 px of a screen edge. Edge: the real-device check (iPhone Safari, Android Chrome) stays unticked for the user. An agent can't run it.

issues.title: F17 · Click to pick up, click to drop
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** F17
### Summary
Holding a trackpad down to drag is hard on laptops.
### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)
Given a print on a laptop, when it is clicked, the pointer moved and clicked again, then the print moves with no button held. Edge: Esc puts it back. Arrow keys move a focused print.

issues.title: F16 · A print can't get stuck
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** F16
### Summary
Prints get stuck at the outer edge of a screen and on the shared edge between joined screens.
### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)
Outer edge: a drag ended by `pointercancel` or lost pointer capture puts the print back where it started. A print always keeps 40 px on screen. Shared edge: a print belongs to the screen its centre is on and snaps fully onto it, with a small buffer so it doesn't flick back. If the other screen can't take it, it snaps back. Edge: "Tidy up" brings every print back into view.

issues.title: R4 · Chaos options for the browser test
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** R4
### Summary
Builds on #35 (timings). Lets us measure loss before changing the design.
### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)
`npm run test:browsers -- --drop 10` drops 10% of relay frames. Other options stop a holder halfway, delay a device and corrupt a piece. Each run writes JSON: time to arrive, bytes sent compared with the file size, pieces asked again and whether the SHA-256 matched. Edge: with `--drop 0` the results match a normal run. Blocked by #35.

issues.title: R1 · A hash for every piece
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** R1 · **Threat IDs:** T-T5
### Summary
Today a bad piece is only found when the whole file fails its SHA-256. Needed before pieces can come from several holders (T-T5).
### Acceptance (the attack fails)
A print carries a hash per piece, signed by the original sender. A corrupted piece is dropped as it arrives and asked again, without fetching the whole file. Edge: a valid file still passes its whole-file SHA-256. Blocked by #24.

issues.title: C12 · Ask another holder and keep pieces when the link changes
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** C12 · **Threat IDs:** T-D4
### Summary
Found in today's code (ARCHITECTURE.md 13): `need` always goes to the first sender even when other holders are listed. A change of piece size (direct to relay) throws away the pieces already received.
### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)
Given a transfer from A with B also holding the file, when A goes silent, then the missing pieces are asked from B and the photo arrives with the right SHA-256. Edge: a link that falls back from direct to relay keeps the pieces it already has.

issues.title: S20 · Remember devices (trust on first use)
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** S20 · **Threat IDs:** T-S8, T-I12
### Summary
Off by default. Lets people notice a new device using a friend's name (T-S8).
### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)
Given "Remember this device" turned on, when the device joins again tomorrow, then others who saw it show "seen before". Edge: a different device using that name shows "new device". Devices that never turned it on aren't stored by anyone. Forget clears this device's keys and everything it stored. Blocked by #24.

issues.title: S19 · Names are unique in a room
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** S19 · **Threat IDs:** T-S6
### Summary
Look-alike names let someone pass as a friend (T-S6).
### Acceptance (the attack fails)
While "Sam" is in the room, "sam", "SAM", "Ｓａｍ" and " Sam " are refused with "Someone in this room is already called Sam". No name is suggested. Names with a zero-width space, a text-direction override or Latin mixed with Cyrillic ("Ѕam") are refused, following UTS #39 "Highly Restrictive". Edge: "Sam M" and "山田さくら" are allowed. Devanagari vowel signs aren't stripped, so different names don't clash. "👩‍👩‍👧" is allowed and counts as one character. Two devices picking "Sam" at once: the time keeper keeps the first.

issues.title: S18 · A reload is the same device coming back
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** S18 · **Threat IDs:** T-I8
### Summary
Today a reload makes a new device: joins break and transfers start over.
### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)
Given a joined device halfway through a transfer, when its page reloads, then it comes back with the same id, name and colour, still joined. The transfer finishes. Edge: received files stay in memory only, so the transfer restarts from a holder. A duplicated tab can't get the Web Lock on its tab id and starts as a new device. After a tab closes, the next start-up deletes its stored keys (ARCHITECTURE.md 6.1).

Prints, join tabs, the mini-map and messages have spoken labels and arrivals are announced. Animation is reduced when the device asks for it. Edge: a VoiceOver pass on a real iPhone stays unticked for the user.

**PRD ID:** F13
### Summary
One tap saves every received photo.

Given 12 received photos on a phone, when "Save all" is tapped, then the share sheet opens once with all 12. On a laptop they download. Edge: real-device check on iPhone and Android stays unticked for the user.

issues.title: F12 · Share with everyone
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** F12 · **Threat IDs:** T-D10
### Summary
A "For everyone" tray and a "Share with everyone" option on every print.
### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)
Given five devices with two joined, when Sam drops a print on the tray, then all four others receive it, joined or not. Edge: the 20 MB limit from F11 applies.

issues.title: F11 · Joined screens receive by themselves
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** F11 · **Threat IDs:** T-S7, T-D10
### Summary
Nobody in a joined group should have to drag each photo.
### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)
Given three joined screens, when Sam drops a photo into the space, then both others fetch it with no drag and show "1 new photo from Sam". Edge: nothing is fetched by itself until the join has settled (accepted, or 10 s with no Undo), and prints from before the join need a tap. A 30 MB file isn't fetched by itself ("30 MB. Tap to get it"). Prints from devices outside the group aren't fetched by themselves.

issues.title: C16 · Mini-map to arrange screens
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** C16 · **Threat IDs:** T-S7
### Summary
Every device in the room as a tile. Each person moves only their own. The accessible way to join and the way to fix a wrong join.
### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)
Given three devices, when Ali places their tile below Sam's and taps Done, then Sam sees "Ali wants to join below you" and nothing joins until Sam taps Accept. Edge: "No" leaves both as they were. Tiles move with arrow keys.

issues.title: C15 · Join screens by tapping join tabs
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** C15 · **Threat IDs:** T-S7
### Summary
Replaces the orb push (C2 withdrawn): orbs dragged to the edge clash with the phone's edge gestures and are awkward on a trackpad.
### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)
Given two devices in a room, when each clicks the join tab on facing edges within 2 s, then both show "Joined with <name>, on your right" with Undo and behave as one space. Edge: tabs that don't face each other, or taps 3 s apart, don't join. Undo splits them. Tabs sit inset from the bezel, work by keyboard and have spoken labels.

issues.title: C5 · A device can miss the layout when the time keeper leaves
issues.body:
**PRD ID:** C5 (the layout when a screen leaves) · **Threat IDs:** T-S5 (the hand-over must not let a stranger take the role)

### What happened
The two-browser test timed out twice on 13 Nov at the same step, the late guest joining after the time keeper leaves (`tests/two-browser.mjs:288`, `await until(C, () => window.__t.net.joins.length === 1, …)`). It passes on other runs with no code change. Found by the unattended agent on #41, which traced it from the code; it hasn't been reproduced on purpose yet.

### Likely cause (from reading `web/net.js`)
1. A, the time keeper, leaves. B becomes the time keeper and sends its layout.
2. C may not have heard that A left yet, so it still treats A as the time keeper and drops B's layout (`payload.from !== s.leader`, `web/net.js:130`).
3. B doesn't send it again, so C's joins stay empty.

### Acceptance
- When the time keeper changes, every device ends up with the new time keeper's layout, whatever order they hear about it in.
- A layout from a device that isn't the time keeper is still dropped (Rule 1).

### Edge cases
- Two devices hear about the leave in opposite orders.
- The new time keeper leaves straight away.

### Must not break
- `npm run test:browsers`, direct and relay: every check still passes.

### How to test
In the two-browser test, delay C's presence update so it hears about A leaving after B has sent its layout. C still ends up with B's layout. The late-guest step must also wait for C to see that A has gone, as well as B, but only together with the fix, or the test would just hide the bug.

issues.body:

issues.title: S2 · Devices can't impersonate each other
issues.body:
### Summary
Anyone can send messages "from B" and swap B's key (T-S1). Fix: a device's id is the first 128 bits of SHA-256(public key) in base64url (22 characters), with a format check in `isDevId`. All setup after the key is sealed: the WebRTC offer carries the DTLS fingerprint, so sealing it is what stops the direct-link hijack.
### Acceptance (the attack fails)
A key that doesn't hash to its id is dropped. A forged "from B" setup from a third browser is dropped and A links to the real B. Edge: B leaves and rejoins with a new key and still connects. Scope: device messages only. Room messages go with S1.1 and S1.4. Ids not in the room are #21.

### Update (PR #50, design review)
- A device has two key pairs: encryption (ECDH P-256) and signing (ECDSA P-256). Its id is the first 128 bits of the SHA-256 of **both** public keys, so nobody can attach their own signing key to another device's id (ARCHITECTURE.md, Keys).
- Room messages are signed with the ECDSA key and checked against the key bound to the id. No signed message is accepted until the keys match the id.
- A colour and three emoji made from the id are shown next to each name, as a visual aid only.

issues.title: S1.5 · Rate-limit resend requests per device
issues.body:
### Summary
A device that keeps asking for the same file makes the sender upload it again and again, up to 200 MB each time (T-D3). It floods the room's relay and the sender's data.

### Acceptance (the attack fails)
- Per device and per file, whole-file sends are allowed at most 3 times in any 60 seconds. A whole-file send is a `want`, a `need` with no list of pieces, or a `need` whose list covers more than half the file's pieces. Requests over the limit are dropped and nothing is sent.
- Requests for a few missing pieces (a `need` listing half the pieces or fewer) are allowed at most once a second per device per file. The receiver's own retries are 1.5–3 s apart, so they're never dropped.
- Dropped requests don't count towards the limit, so a device can't keep itself locked out.
- Requests for a file this device doesn't have are dropped before they're counted.
- The counters are bounded: they're cleared when a device leaves and capped in number. The limits are named constants in `LIMITS` (Rule 3).

### Edge cases
- A real transfer that loses pieces on the relay still finishes: its retries stay under the limit.
- The limit is per device: a second device asking for the same file still gets it.
- After 60 seconds the same device can ask again.

### Must not break
- `npm run test:browsers`, direct and relay: every check still passes, including the late guest's download and the silent-device timeout.

### How to test the attack
In the two-browser test, B sends A 20 `want` messages for the same photo within a second, then 20 `need` messages listing every piece within a second. Each time A sends the file at most 3 times (count A's outgoing sends for that photo). A third device then asks once and still gets the file.

issues.title: S1.4 · Only accept clock replies from the time keeper
issues.body:
### Summary
A fake clock reply can stop a device joining screens (T-D5).
### Acceptance (the attack fails)
A forged clock reply doesn't change anyone's clock.
### Blocked by #24
A clock reply is sent as `{ to, t0, t1 }`, with no sender, and broadcasts don't say who sent them. Any "only from the time keeper" check could be forged until devices can prove who they are (S2, #24).

issues.title: S1.2 · Limits apply per device, not per room
issues.body:
### Summary
One device can fill the room-wide transfer and print limits (T-D2).
### Acceptance (the attack fails)
One device reaching its limit doesn't stop anyone else's photos.

issues.title: S1.1 · The time keeper can't be chosen by lying about join time
issues.body:

### Acceptance (the attack fails)
A device claiming an early join time doesn't become time keeper, also after the host reloads.
